data: 地球[ちきゅう] 温暖[おんだん]化[か]の 問題[もんだい]は もっと 大[おお]きくなっていくのでは ないでしょうか。
Isn't the problem of global warming going to keep growing bigger from now on?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This ending indicates the speaker's conjecture and is used to express an opinion in an indecisive fashion. Although the negative form ではない is used, there is no negative meaning. のではない{だろう/でしょう}か are used only in written language, and のではないだろうか is the more formal form. ん{ではないでしょうか/じゃないかな} are used only in spoken language. んじゃないかな is more casual. --- 英訳 [English translation]: I think that ~; Isn't it that~? --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Sのではないでしょうか。
今[いま]、 食[た]べたばかりですから, お腹[なか]が いっぱいで、 何[なに]も 食[た]べられません。
I just ate, and I'm so full that I really can't eat another bite.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-plain.past ばかり indicates that someone has just done something or something has just happened. The noun modification form is ばかりの. --- 英訳 [English translation]: have just V-ed --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.past ばかりだ V-plain.past ばかりの N
作文[さくぶん]は ワープロで 書[か]いても いい はずだが、 一応[いちおう]、 先生[せんせい]に 聞[き]いてみよう。
It should be fine to use a word processor to write the composition, but let's ask the teacher, just in case.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

一応 "for the time being; for now; tentatively; although not perfectly; sort of; just in case" In this sentence the use means "tentatively" 一応 is used when an action/state is tentative or not quite complete, perfect or satisfactory. It is also used when an action is taken as a precaution.
この 本[ほん]は、 話[はな]し言葉[ことば]的[てき] 表現[ひょうげん]で 書[か]かれているので、 とても 分[わ]かりやすい。
This book is written in a colloquial style, so it's very easy to understand.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N+的 the suffix is attached to nouns to make them な-adjectives. When these adj modify nouns, the な is sometimes omitted.
この 問題[もんだい]を いかに 解決[かいけつ] すべきか、 みんなで 話[はな]し合[あ]わなくては ならない。
We all need to discuss how we should solve this problem.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
いかに〜か "how; how much; in what way" This structure occurs as an embedded interrogative sentence, where いかに means "how (much)" or "in what way". This structure is commonly used in written language.
調査[ちょうさ]に よると、 この 大学[だいがく]での 大学[だいがく]院[いん]生[せい]の 割合[わりあい]は 25[にじゅうご]％と なっています。
According to the survey, it turns out that 25% of this university's student population are graduate students.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

AはBとなっている。 where B = Noun or noun equivalent such as "# + counter" or "N + Prt" Meaning: happen to be; it turns out that ~; it's been decided that~; the rule is that ~ indicates that what is stated in the preceding AはB sentence is something beyond the speaker's control. The sentence is often findings or matters decided by others. Note that だ does not occur after B in the sentence.
この 大学[だいがく]の ビジネス学[がく] 部[ぶ]は、 医学[いがく] 部[ぶ]と 並[なら]んでは いるのが 難[むずか]しいらしい。
I hear that the business school at this university, just like the medical school, is hard to get into.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N と並んで "as well as; just like" Is used when introducing one or more examples to be compared to the subject of the sentence. It is used primarily in written language.
だいたいの 数[かず]は 分[わ]かりますが、 正確[せいかく]な 数[かず]は 調[しら]べてみないと 分[わ]かりません。
We have approximate figures, but we'll have to do some research to get an accurate count.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
だいたい number/amount "approximately number/amount" だいたい means "most;almost; nearly(all); approximate." The meaning changes depending on what だいたい modifies.
オリンピックを する ことに 決[き]まってから、 その 国[くに]は 国際[こくさい]的[てき]になってきた。
Since it was decided that it would host the Olympics, that country has become more cosmopolitan.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N+的 the suffix is attached to nouns to make them な-adjectives. When these adj modify nouns, the な is sometimes omitted.
量[りょう]は 多[おお]かったけれど、 お腹[なか]が すいていたから、 ほとんど 食[た]べてしまった。
There was a lot of food, but I was hungry, so I ate almost all of it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
ほとんど V Means "almost all; most of (it, the time, etc.)" It is only used with the amount of something is the issue.
B型[がた]の 性格[せいかく]は 楽天[らくてん]なのに 対[たい]して、 A型[がた]は まじめな 性格[せいかく]だと 言[い]われている。
It is said that people with blood type B are optimistic, whereas people with blood type A are serious.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
Sのに対して "whereas; on the other hand; in contrast" に対して is used when contrasting two actions, states, situations, etc.
アラビア語[ご]は、 日本[にほん]語[ご]や ロシア語[ご]と 並[なら]んで 難[むずか]しい 言葉[ことば]だと 言[い]われている。
Arabic, along with languages like Japanese and Russian, is said to be a difficult language to learn.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N と並んで "as well as; just like" Is used when introducing one or more examples to be compared to the subject of the sentence. It is used primarily in written language.
日本[にほん]での インターンシップの 経験[けいけん]は、 私[わたし]の 人生[じんせい]を 大[おお]きく 左右[さゆう] するだろう。
My internship experience in Japan will probably have a big impact on my life.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1 を N2 左右する "influence; govern" 左右する is most commonly used in written language.
私[わたし]の 知[し]っている 限[かぎ]り、 外国[がいこく]人[じん]が 使[つか]いやすい 日本[にほん]語[ご]の 辞書[じしょ]は ないんですよ。
As far as I know, there's no Japanese dictionary that's easy for non-native speakers to use.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain 限り "as long as; as far as; while; until; unless; as much as; as much as (one can)" this grammar is used when something is the case or is true as long as the condition in X holds true. It is also used to indicate the extent to which one can do something or one knows something. (as far as one can; as far as one knows)
家[いえ]に 帰[かえ]って 初[はじ]めて カバンの 中[なか]の 財布[さいふ]が なくなっている ことに 気[き]が ついた。
It was when I returned home that I first realized that my wallet had disappeared from my bag.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S ことに気がつく means: notice (that~); realize that ~ Notice that the presence of こと in a sentence using this grammar may not always be the nominalizer meaning "that." It could be a noun meaning "thing" following the noun-typed usage of this grammar.
両親[りょうしん]が 亡[な]くなった 後[あと]、 私[わたし]は 兄[あに]と ともに 二人[ふたり]で 助[たす]け合[あ]って 生[い]きてきました。
Since my parents died, my older brother and I have gotten by together, just the two of us, helping each other.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
Nと共に "with; along with; as" indicates that someone does something or that something happens with N.
ハワイは １[いち]年[ねん] 中気[ちゅうき]温[おん]が 高[たか]いけれど、 高[たか]い 山[やま]では 雪[ゆき]が 降[ふ]る 事[こと]も 有[あ]る そうだ。
Hawaii is warm all year around, but I hear that there are times when it snows in the high mountains.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-plain-nonpast ことがある is used when something occurs (or someone does something) occasionally. も implies that something else may also occur. Note: This phrase should not be confused with V-plain-PAST ことがある (e.g. 日本に行ったことがある。) which states previous experience. --- 英訳 [English translation]: There are times when ~, sometimes --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain-nonpast こと{が / も}ある
日本[にほん]に 留学[りゅうがく] した 経験[けいけん]を 生[い]かして、 大学[だいがく]の 留学[りゅうがく] アドバイザーに なる つもりだ。
I intend to make the most of my experience studying abroad in Japan and become a study-abroad adviser at a university.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
生かす "make the most of; make the best use of; use effectively; maintain" 生かす means literally "to keep alive," but it is also used to mean "to make the most of one's ability, etc"
日本[にほん]に 留学[りゅうがく]中[ちゅう]は、 ホームステイの 家族[かぞく]を はじめ 色々[いろいろ]な 人[ひと]に お世話[せわ]に なった。
When I was studying in Japan, a lot of people helped me out, starting with my host family.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: Noun をはじめ is used to present a primary example when mentioning a group of things or people. --- 英訳 [English translation]: beginning with~; starting with ~; including ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nをはじめ
日本[にほん]語[ご]では、 目上[めうえ]の 人[ひと]に 対[たい]して 「あなた」と 呼[よ]ぶのは とても 失礼[しつれい]な ことだ。
In Japanese, it's very rude to address your superiors as "anata".
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N に対して "toward; for; in; with regard to" This grammar marks something to/toward/about which one does something, or mark someone to/toward whom one does something or owes something. In different contexts, it can mark something one has interest in. Do not confuse with the use where に対して indicates two contrasting actions, states, situations, etc.
私[わたし]は 健康[けんこう]の ため、 エレベーターに 乗[の]らないで 階段[かいだん]を 使[つか]う ことに しています。
To maintain my health, I make a habit of taking the stairs instead of the elevator.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: When ため(に) is preceded by a noun or the non-past form of a verb, it indicates either purpose or reason/cause. In different contexts, Noun のため(に) also indicates benefit, as seen in the example sentence in this flashcard. --- 英訳 [English translation]: in order to; to; for the purpose of; for; for the sake of --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nのため(に) N1のためのN2 Verb plainため(に) Verb plainためのN
天気[てんき] 予報[よほう]は、 今日[きょう]は 雨[あめ]だと 言[い]っていた。 ところが、 とても いい 天気[てんき]に なった。
The weather forecast said that it would rain today, but we ended up having beautiful weather.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ところが is a sentence initial conjunction used when something takes place which is unexpected from the preceding context. The sentence after ところが represents an event or action the speaker cannot control. --- 英訳 [English translation]: however; but; nevertheless --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ S１。ところが S２ where S1=what's expected; S2= what actually occurred.
この 情報[じょうほう]を 見[み]るには、 この ソフトウェアを インストール する 必要[ひつよう]が あります。
In order to view this information, it is necessary to install this software.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain.non-past.aff には "to; in order to; for; for the purpose of; when" には indicates purpose in general statements (often stating the speaker's judgement about an action in terms of its effectiveness, convenience, necessity, etc.). には can also mean "when" (=時には). Verbs or nouns can precede には. Note that when ために is used, the predicate in the main clause describes an action. Such that: Xには Y, where Y is a judgment and never an action XためにY, where Y is an action and never a judgement. AND, XためにはY, where Y is a judgment, never an action
なんだ、 まだ 宿題[しゅくだい] 終[お]わってないの。 早[はや]くしないと、 授業[じゅぎょう]が はじまっちゃうよ。
Oh, you're not done with your homework yet? Hurry up; class is about to start.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
なんだ "oh!" The literal meaning of なんだ is "What is X?" However it can also be used to express the speaker's slight surprise。 Used only in very casual conversation.
この 大学[だいがく]の 学生[がくせい]である 限[かぎ]り、 大学[だいがく]が 決[き]めた ルールは 守[まも]らなくては いけません。
As long as you're a student here, you have to abide by the university's rules.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain 限り "as long as; as far as; while; until; unless; as much as; as much as (one can)" this grammar is used when something is the case or is true as long as the condition in X holds true. It is also used to indicate the extent to which one can do something or one knows something. (as far as one can; as far as one knows)
子供[こども]向[む]けに 作[つく]られた 映画[えいが]の 中[なか]にも、 大人[おとな]が 見[み]ても 楽[たの]しい ものが たくさん ある。
There are lots of films that, although made for children, are still enjoyable for adults to watch.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N 向けに V Means: for; made for; for the use of; directed to The suffix 向け adds the meaning "made for; for the use of; directed toward." 向け is often affixed to nouns which refer to people, countries and organizations.
北海道[ほっかいどう]の ホスト ファミリーの お母[かあ]さんは 元気[げんき]かなあ。 今晩[こんばん]、 電話[でんわ] してみよう。
I wonder how my host mom in Hokkaido is. I'll try giving her a call tonight.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 〜かなあ is a sentence final particle which indicates that the sentence is a self-addressed question or a question addressed to the speaker's in-group member(s). It is used only in casual language. --- 英訳 [English translation]: I wonder ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜かな(あ)
毎晩[まいばん] コーラス 部[ぶ]の 練習[れんしゅう]が 有[あ]るので、 勉強[べんきょう]を し始[はじ]めるのは いつも １０[じゅう]時[じ]過[す]ぎだ。
Because I have practice at chorus club every night, I always start studying after 10:00.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
説明 [explanation]: 始める in this use is an auxiliary verb meaning "begin to V." --- 英訳 [English translation]: begin to, begin-V-ing --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Verb-masu 始める
この 大学[だいがく]では、 日本[にほん]語[ご]、 あるいは、 英語[えいご]で 卒業[そつぎょう] 論文[ろんぶん]を 書[か]く ことに なっている。
At this university, senior theses are expected to be written in either Japanese or English.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1(、N2、〜）あるいは Nn "or; either ~ or ~" あるいは is used to connect alternatives. It is usually used in formal speech or written language.
将来[しょうらい]は、 ヨーロッパ、 あるいは、 アジアで 仕事[しごと]が できたらいいと 思[おも]っている。
I think it'd be nice if I could work in Europe or Asia in the future.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1(、N2、〜）あるいは Nn "or; either ~ or ~" あるいは is used to connect alternatives. It is usually used in formal speech or written language.
試験[しけん]に 合格[ごうかく] できた 第[だい]一[いち]の 理由[りゆう]は、 覚[おぼ]えた 言葉[ことば]や 漢字[かんじ]が 全部[ぜんぶ] 試験[しけん]に 出[で]た ことだ。
The primary reason I passed the test is that all the words and kanji I memorized were on it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
第一 のN "first; first of all; to begin with; the first; the primary"
父[ちち]は １０[じゅう]年[ねん] 前[まえ]に 亡[な]くなった。 それ 以来[いらい]、 母[はは]は 一人[ひとり]で 私[わたし]達[たち] 兄弟[きょうだい]を 育[そだ]ててくれた。
My father passed away ten years ago. Since then, my mother has reared my brother and me on her own.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
VN/Nいらい "since ~" It is used with V-te or VN referring to an action in the past, or with N indicating a specific time in the past.
今年[ことし]は 12[じゅうに]月[がつ]に なっても なかなか 寒[さむ]くならない。 地球[ちきゅう] 温暖[おんだん]化[か]の せいだろうか。
This year it just hasn't gotten cold even though it's already December. I wonder if it's because of global warming.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

なかなか V-nai ない "not easily; not readily; difficult to~; slow to; to refuse to" なかなか with V-nai is usually used when something desirable doesn't happen easily or when something that is supposed to happen doesn't happen.
プレイスメント テストに 合格[ごうかく] しない 限[かぎ]り、 上[うえ]の レベルの クラスには 入[い]れません。
You won't be able to take upper-level classes until you pass the placement test.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain 限り "as long as; as far as; while; until; unless; as much as; as much as (one can)" this grammar is used when something is the case or is true as long as the condition in X holds true. It is also used to indicate the extent to which one can do something or one knows something. (as far as one can; as far as one knows)
世界[せかい]で 一番[いちばん] 長[なが]い 川[かわ]は ナイルだと 言[い]われているが、 アマゾン川[かわ]だと 言[い]う 人[ひと]も 居[い]る。
The Nile river is said to be the longest river in the world, but there are also people who say it is the Amazon river.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to introduce something commonly said about something or someone. --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~ it is said to be ~, It is said that ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ーはSentence-plainと言われている
もう かなり 歩[ある]いた はずなのに、 まだ 目的[もくてき] 地[ち]に 着[つ]かない。 道[みち]に 迷[まよ]ったのだろうか。
We must have walked quite far already, but we still haven't reached our destination. I wonder if we're lost.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
かなり "considerably; rather; quite; fairly; pretty; quite a lot; Indicates that the degree of something is not extremely high, but is higher than average.
この 公園[こうえん]は 地図[ちず]の 上[うえ]では 家[いえ]から 近[ちか]い ように 見[み]えるが、 歩[ある]くと 結構[けっこう] 時間[じかん]が かかる。
On a map this park looks close to the house, but when you walk there it takes quite a while.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N のうえで "in terms of; from the viewpoint of ~; as far as ~ is concerned; according to ~" Nの上で and N上 are used to indicate that the speaker's statement refers only to N. Commonly used in written language.
道後[どうご] 温泉[おんせん]は 日本[にほん]の 一番[いちばん] 古[ふる]い 温泉[おんせん]で、 ３０００[さんぜん]年[ねん]の 歴史[れきし]が 有[あ]ると 言[い]われています。
It is said that the Dougo Onsen, with 3000 years of history, is the oldest onsen in Japan.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to introduce something commonly said about something or someone. --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~ it is said to be ~, It is said that ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ーはSentence-plainと言われている
この 論文[ろんぶん]は すばらしいと 思[おも]う。 しかしながら、 賛成[さんせい] できない 点[てん]も いくつか ある。
I think this is an excellent paper. However, there are a few points with which I cannot agree.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S1. しかしながら S2. "however, but" しかしながら is a disjunctive conjunction and appears only in sentence-initial position. It is a highly formal expression and is used typically in written language.
コンビニには、 生活[せいかつ] 用品[ようひん]でも 食[た]べ物[もの]でも 雑誌[ざっし]や 新聞[しんぶん]でも、 なんでも 置[お]いてある。
They've got everything at convenience stores, from everyday essentials to food to magazines and newspapers.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1 でも N2 でも "including X and Y; whether (it is) X or Y" This is used to provide examples for the statement in the sentence. This structure implies that there are also things other than the examples which make the statement true. Note that XもYも (both X and Y) does not carry such an implication..
この アパートは 駅[えき]に 近[ちか]くて 便利[べんり]な ことは 便利[べんり]だけれど、 家賃[やちん]は とても 高[たか]いです。
It's true that this apartment is close to the station and is convenient, but the rent is really high.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

ANa {な/だった} ことは ANa {だ/だった} が "It is certainly true that ~, but; indeed ~, but; do V ~, but; ~ is/are/was/etc. ~, but" This structure is used when the speaker/writer admits that the proposition is true but wants to qualify the proposition with an additional remark.
この ノートに 書[か]いてある ことは 全部[ぜんぶ] 覚[おぼ]えたと 思[おも]うが、 一応[いちおう]、 もう 一度[いちど] 見[み]ておこう。
I think I've memorized everything written in this notebook, but I'll take another look, just in case.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

一応 "for the time being; for now; tentatively; although not perfectly; sort of; just in case" In this sentence the use means "tentatively" 一応 is used when an action/state is tentative or not quite complete, perfect or satisfactory. It is also used when an action is taken as a precaution.
登録[とうろく] した 学生[がくせい]が 少[すく]ないと いう 理由[りゆう]で、 その 授業[じゅぎょう]は キャンセル されてしまいました。
Because there were too few students registered for it, that class ended up being cancelled.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S-plain という理由で "because" (lit. for the reason that~) is used to present the reason for a state, event, or action stated in the main clause. The phrase is usually used in written language.
会議[かいぎ]が 始[はじ]まってから もう 3[さん]時間[じかん] 以上[いじょう] 経[た]っている。 いったい いつ 終[お]わるのだろうか。
It's already been more than three hours since the meeting began. When on earth will it end?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

いったい QW "(what, who, where, how, etc.) on earth" いったい is an intensifier used with questions. It usually occurs immediately preceding the question word, but it may appear in other locations before the QW.
日本[にほん] 経済[けいざい] 新聞[しんぶん]や ウォール ストリート ジャーナルには、 ビジネス向[む]けの 記事[きじ]が 多[おお]い。
In papers like Nihon Keizai Shinbun and the Wall Street Journal, many articles are written with businesspeople in mind.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N 向けの N2. Means: for; made for; for the use of; directed to The suffix 向け adds the meaning "made for; for the use of; directed toward." 向け is often affixed to nouns which refer to people, countries and organizations.
図書[としょ]館[かん]で 1[いち]時間[じかん]ぐらい かかって、 ついに その 本[ほん]を 探[さが]し出[だ]した 時[とき]は、 うれしかった。
I was happy when I finally found the book after spending about an hour at the library searching for it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S1 一方（で）、S2. "While; when; at the same time; on the other hand" The conjunction 一方 is used to present two contrastive situations or two concurrent states, events or actions. 一方 is usually used in written language.
東京[とうきょう]、 大阪[おおさか] ともに 外国[がいこく]人[じん]が 多[おお]い 町[まち]だ。
There are a lot of foreigners in both Tokyo and Osaka.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1,N2 共（に） "Both N1 and N2" The colloquial form is N1もN2も.
大阪[おおさか]、 京都[きょうと]、 それに 奈良[なら]にも 行[おこな]った。
I went to Osaka, Kyoto, and Nara as well.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: それに is used to add an item or make an addition statement. --- 英訳 [English translation]: in addition; moreover; furthermore; what's more; on top of that; and --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N1 {、/と / に} N2, それに N3 b. S1。それに、S2。 c. S1 し、それに、S2。
大阪[おおさか]まで 新[しん]幹線[かんせん]で 行[い]きたいんですが、 いくらでしょうか。
I would like to go as far as Osaka by bullet train. How much does it cost?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: S んだけど／ですが is used as a preliminary remark by the speaker to inform the hearer of the speaker's desire, the current situation, etc. before (a) asking a question related to that desire, (b) asking for an opinion on the matter, or (c) making a request. This phrase can also be used to extend an invitation or an offer. When making a request, the request is often unstated, as shown below. んだけど is more casual than んですが. --- 英訳 [English translation]: but (in english, null in most situations) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜ん{だけど/ですが}
今週[こんしゅう]中[ちゅう]に メールを 出[だ]すか 電話[でんわ]を 掛[か]けるか しますから、 待[ま]っていて下[くだ]さい。
I'll either e-mail you or call you some time this week, so please wait for that.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The phrase AかBか is used to present alternatives. When Bか is followed by a case particle (e.g., が, を, へ, に, で, と), the second か is usually dropped. --- 英訳 [English translation]: either A or B; whether A or B --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. 〜か〜か b. N1かN2+Particle
同[おな]じ 漢字[かんじ] また 間違[まちが]えた。
I got the same kanji wrong again.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: In addition to the meaning "again," また expresses the meaning "also" or "additionally." --- 英訳 [English translation]: also; as well; additionally; in addition; moreover --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ また、S。
性格[せいかく]は 人[ひと]に よって 違[ちが]います。
Character/personality differs depending on the person.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to indicate that something differs depending on the situation, location, time, etc. --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~によって違う = differ depending on ~ / due to ~ による = depend on, due to, according to --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {Noun/Question Word ~ か/ ~かどうか}は Noun に {よって違う / よる }
この 岩[いわ]を 磨[みが]き上[あ]げてください。
Please polish up this rock.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

磨き上げる (V-masu 上げる） transitive "to polish up; to shine up" Affixed to the masu-stems of verbs, 上げる forms compound verbs, adding meanings such as "finish something up," "upward" or "to a great extent." the meaning is determined by the preceding verb.
彼[かれ]と 私[わたし]の 考[かんが]えは まったく 同[おな]じだ。
His idea and mine are exactly the same.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

まったく {V/A/ANo/(の)N/Ano} "totally; utterly; entirely; completely; extremely; absolutely; really" used for emphasis in affirmative sentences. often used to express the speaker's emotion. In negative sentences, it indicates complete negation. It is used with verbs (often in potential form) and i-adjectives in negative sentences. まったく〜（という）わけではない indicates partial negation.
日本[にほん]に 引[ひ]っ越[こ]す ことに なりました。
It's been decided that I'll move to Japan.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-non-pastことになった means that a situation has changed due to some external force (e.g. a decision made by someone other than the speaker). It indicates either that the speaker (or the subject of the sentence) did not actively make the decision or that he/she is viewing the decision from the standpoint of an outsider. Note that ことにした indicates that the speaker or the subject made a decision to do something. --- 英訳 [English translation]: It was/has been decided that ~; It turns out that~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-non-past.plain-ことになった:{行く/行かない}ことになった
１８[じゅうはっ]歳[さい] 以上[いじょう]の 人[ひと]しか 見[み]られません。
Only people who are 18 or older can watch.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: X以上 and X以下 means "equal to or more than X" and "(equal to or) less than X," respectively. A Number + Counter or a demonstrative pronoun such as これ and それ commonly occurs before 以上 and 以下. When the topic is academic grades, grade symbols such as C and B can be used (e.g., C以上). --- 英訳 [English translation]: 以上 = or more 以下 = less than; or less --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Number (+ Counter) 以上/以下: ３年生以上 b. Demonstrative pronoun 以上/以下: これ以上; それ以下
あの 小娘[こむすめ]は、 まるで 子猫[こねこ]の ようだ。
That young girl is just like a kitten.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

Sentence ending form: 〜ようだ。 "as if ~ (were/-ed); just like" This structure is used to introduce a simile, i.e., to describe a thing, person, action, etc. by comparing it with a similar thing, person, action, etc. まるで is an emphatic marker.
疲[つか]れていて 話[はなし]も できないほどだった。
We were so tired we couldn't even speak.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain.non-past ほど "to the extent that~ ; so~ that ~ (almost)~; not as ~ as N; to (this/that) degree; (this/that) much" The particle ほど is used to express the degree of a state. When a sentence precedes ほど, the element just before ほど is a verb.
友達[ともだち]が 迎[むか]えに 来[き]たら、 私[わたし]は 帰[かえ]ります。
If/when my friend comes to pick me up, I will leave.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S1たらS２。 When たら is used, as opposed to (の)なら, S1 must be completed before S2. 説明 [explanation]: なら is used when the speaker supposes that something is the case or is true and makes a statement, suggestion, etc. based on that supposition. の occurs before なら when the supposition is based on what the speaker has heard from someone or learned from the situation. Nなら means "if it is N; N would/could ~." In "S1 なら S2", the action/event in S1 does not have to take place before that in S2. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Nなら = would; could~ S(の)なら = if (it's the case that) ~; if (it's true that) ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ~(の)なら
この カレーは 辛[つら]くて 涙[なみだ]が 出[で]るほどだ。
This curry is so spicy it brings tears to your eyes.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain.non-past ほど "to the extent that~ ; so~ that ~ (almost)~; not as ~ as N; to (this/that) degree; (this/that) much" The particle ほど is used to express the degree of a state. When a sentence precedes ほど, the element just before ほど is a verb.
私[わたし]たちは 話[はなし]も 出来[でき]ないほど 疲[つか]れていた。
We were so tired we couldn't even speak.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain.non-past ほど "to the extent that~ ; so~ that ~ (almost)~; not as ~ as N; to (this/that) degree; (this/that) much" The particle ほど is used to express the degree of a state. When a sentence precedes ほど, the element just before ほど is a verb.
明日[あした]の コンサート、 一緒[いっしょ]に 行[い]くだろう。
You're going with me to the concert tomorrow, right?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: でしょう and だろう with rising intonation are used to elicit the hearer's confirmation. でしょう is the polite version of だろう. In casual conversation, male speakers use だろう and female speakers use でしょう. In more casual situations, the final う tends to drop. Note: でしょう and だろう with falling intonation indicate conjecture. --- 英訳 [English translation]: tag question(e.g. isn't it?; wasn't it?; aren't they?; is he?; are they?) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ~だろう, ~でしょう
腹[はら]の 立[た]つ ことには、 私[わたし]、 彼[かれ]が 好[す]きです。
What makes me angry is that I like him.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V.plain ことに “It is~ that~; I am/We are ~ that ~; To my ~" ことに is used to express the speaker's feeling or subjective judgment about what is said in the main clause. ことに can only be used with a limited set of words.
来月[らいげつ] 山田[やまだ] 先生[せんせい]が 結婚[けっこん] するらしいですよ。
I hear that Professor Yamada is getting married next month.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

〜らしい。 Means: seem; apparently; I heard that ~; it looks like The auxiliary i-adjective らしい is used to express the speaker's conjecture based on what he/she has learned through an information source or his/her own observation
忙[いそが]し過[す]ぎて、 寝[ね]る 時間[じかん]さえ ありません。
I'm so busy I don't even have time to sleep.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N (prt) さえ Means: even さえ is an emphatic particle. In non-conditional clauses it means "even." When さえ is used, the particle が never occurs, を usually does not occur, へ and the directional に are optional, and the other particles, including the LOCATIONAL に, で、と and から are mandatory.
もし 文法[ぶんぽう]が 間違[まちが]ってたら、 直[なお]してくれる？
If you find mistakes with the grammar, will you fix them for me?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-te くれる, etc. with rising intonation is used to make request in casual conversation. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Will you ~?; Can you ~?; Could you~? --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-te {くれる / くれない / もらえる / もらえない}
せっかくですが、 今日[きょう]は 仕事[しごと]が 忙[いそが]しくて。
It's kind of you to ask, but I'm busy with work today...
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

せっかく{ですが／ですけど／だけど／etc} "with effort; at great pain; take the trouble to do ~; ~, which is a rare occasion/event/etc." せっかく is used in 2 situations: (2) when a given opportunity is rare and therefore he/she wants to make use of it; or, in spite of their opportunity, he/she cannot make use of it
熱[あつ]い うちに、 どうぞ 召[め]し上[あ]がって下[くだ]さい。
Please go ahead and eat while it's still hot.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (ない)うちに is used when someone does something before a situation or state changes. 間に is used in similar situations, but it cannot be used with the negative forms of verbs. Another difference between the two phrases is that うちに always implies that it is not possible, easy or a good idea to do something after the time specified by the うちに clause. However, this is not always the case with 間に. Thus far, if it is not a problem for the speaker to go to Japan after finishing his Japanese class, 間に should be used, as shown below: 日本語の勉強をしている間に日本に行ってみたい。 --- 英訳 [English translation]: while ~ still ～ないうちに＝ before (something happens) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ～うちに
日本[にほん]の 夏[なつ]は とても 暑[あつ]い。 それに 湿度[しつど]も 高[たか]い。
Japan's summers are very hot. Furthermore, the humidity is also high.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: それに is used to add an item or make an addition statement. --- 英訳 [English translation]: in addition; moreover; furthermore; what's more; on top of that; and --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N1 {、/と / に} N2, それに N3 b. S1。それに、S2。 c. S1 し、それに、S2。
ピクニックの 途中[とちゅう]で、 急[きゅう]に 雨[あめ]が 降[ふ]り出[だ]した。
In the middle of the picnic it suddenly started to rain.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-masu 出す Means: V out; begin to V; start to V; begin V-ing; start V-ing V出す differs from V始める in that V出す is used for abrupt and non-volitional actions, while V始める is used for both volitional and non-volitional actions but NOT for actions which begin abruptly. V-masu 出す has 2 meanings, here is the (2) Someone begins something or something begins
雪[ゆき]さえ 降[ふ]らなければ、 車[くるま]の 運転[うんてん]は 怖[こわ]くない。
As long as it doesn't snow, driving a car isn't scary.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: Noun さえ with a verb conditional form is used when the condition presented in the clause is the only condition to make the statement in the main clause true. さえ replaces が and を in this structure; however, when other particles occur with さえ here, they do not drop. --- 英訳 [English translation]: If~ only ~; If~ just ~; as long as; --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N( = clause X) さえ V-cond (= clause Y)
彼[かれ]は 彼女[かのじょ]と 結婚[けっこん] するべきでは なかったと 思[おも]う。
I think he never should have married her.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V. plain.non-past.aff べき {だ／じゃない／ではない／だった／じゃなかった／ではなかった} "should; ought to" The auxillary べき expresses the speaker's strong judgment that one should do something. The form of する before べき can be either す or する, as in すべき or するべき。
また 朝[あさ] 寝坊[ねぼう] してしまって、 また 授業[じゅぎょう]に 遅[おく]れた。
I overslept again, and again I was late for class.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: In addition to the meaning "again," また expresses the meaning "also" or "additionally." --- 英訳 [English translation]: also; as well; additionally; in addition; moreover --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ また、S。
国民[こくみん]は みんな 税金[ぜいきん]を 払[はら]わなければなりません。
All citizens have to pay taxes.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: These patterns express the idea of obligation. Although the two patterns are interchangeable, there is a subtle difference between ならない and いけない. That is, ならない is commonly used when the speaker states his/her sense of obligation while いけない is commonly used when the sense of obligation is directed towards the hearer (i.e. when the speaker wants to impose a certain obligation on the hearer). The following contracted forms are used in casual conversation: なきゃならない -> なきゃなんない なくちゃならない -> なくちゃんなんない --- 英訳 [English translation]: have to; must; should --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜なければ{いけない/ならない} 〜なくては{いけない/ならない}
橋[はし]の 上[うえ]から 真下[ました]に ある 川[かわ]を 見[み]ると、 とても 怖[こわ]い。
From the bridge, if you look straight down at the river, it's really scary.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

真っX where X = adjective or Noun Means: very; pure; totally; right; mid- 真っAdj indicates the degree of something is very high or is at the highest level. 真っNoun indicates the center of a space or time span. The english translation of 真っ varies according to the word that follows it.
皆[みな]に 聞[き]こえる ように、 大[おお]きい 声[こえ]で 話[はな]して下[くだ]さい。
Please talk in a loud voice so that everyone can hear you.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (1) This construction is used to state either a purpose or the way in which something is to be done. In XようにY, X represents a state or event which is beyond the control of the subject of Y. The verb form before ように is often a potential form or a negative form. (2) In the similar construction XためにY, X represents an action which can be controlled by the subject of Y, while XようにY implies that a certain consequence (X) will arise as the result of an action (Y). --- 英訳 [English translation]: so that ~; in such a way that~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.nonpastように
この カレーは 辛[つら]すぎて、 まったく 食[た]べられない。
This curry is so hot that I can't eat even a bite.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

まったく〜ない "not ~ at all; not ~ in the least" used for emphasis in affirmative sentences. often used to express the speaker's emotion. In negative sentences, it indicates complete negation. It is used with verbs (often in potential form) and i-adjectives in negative sentences. まったく〜（という）わけではない indicates partial negation.
私[わたし]の 家族[かぞく]は、 父[ちち]を はじめ みんな 辛[つら]い 物[もの]が 大好[だいす]きだ。
In my family, everyone loves spicy food, including my dad.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: Noun をはじめ is used to present a primary example when mentioning a group of things or people. --- 英訳 [English translation]: beginning with~; starting with ~; including ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nをはじめ
先月[せんげつ]は 忙[いそが]しくて、 たった 二日[ふつか]しか、 休[やす]めなかった。
Last month was busy; I could take only two days off.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
たった（の）Number (+counter) "only" This is used to emphasize the small amount or number of something.
仕事[しごと]が 忙[いそが]しくても、 昼[ひる]ご飯[はん]だけは 食[た]べて下[くだ]さいね。
Even if you are busy at work, at least eat lunch, OK?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: When the particle は follows a quantifier (i.e., a word such as 3本 or 少し), it adds the meaning "at least." だけは and ぐらいは (or くらいは) after a noun have the same meaning. --- 英訳 [English translation]: at least. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Number (+ Counter) は b. N だけは c. N {ぐらい/くらい}は
原爆[げんばく]の 恐[おそ]ろしさは いまだに 忘[わす]れる ことが できない。
I still can't forget the horrors of the atomic bomb.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
未だに "still; (not ~) yet" indicates that someone of something is in the same state as he/she/it was some time ago. This form is primarily used in written language. In spoken language まだ is used.
私[わたし]は 友達[ともだち]に ノートを 見[み]せてくれる ように 頼[たの]みました。
I asked my friend to show me the notes.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ように頼む/言う is used to quote a request or command indirectly. In an affirmative request ように頼む is often used with てくれる, as in 来てくれるように頼む. (cf. negative request: ~ないように頼む --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~(てくれる)ように頼む = to ask someone to V ~ように言う = to tell someone to V --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. V-non-plast.plain ように頼む/言う b. V-te くれるように頼む c. V-nai ないように頼む/言う
私[わたし]は 友達[ともだち]に 「ノートを 見[み]せて下[くだ]さい」と 頼[たの]みました。
"Please let me see your notes," I asked my friend.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ように頼む/言う is used to quote a request or command indirectly. In an affirmative request ように頼む is often used with てくれる, as in 来てくれるように頼む. (cf. negative request: ~ないように頼む --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~(てくれる)ように頼む = to ask someone to V ~ように言う = to tell someone to V --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. V-non-plast.plain ように頼む/言う b. V-te くれるように頼む c. V-nai ないように頼む/言う
コンピュータの 知識[ちしき]に 関[かん]しては、 彼[かれ]が 一番[いちばん]だと 思[おも]う。
When it comes to knowledge about computers, I think he's the best.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N に関して は S formal "with regard to; concerning; regarding; about; on; related to" について is similar in meaning to に関して, but is less formal and is used in both written and spoken language.
何[なん]だ、 もう 食[た]べちゃったの。 一緒[いっしょ]に 食[た]べたかったのに。
Wait, you already ate? But I wanted to eat together.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
なんだ "oh!" The literal meaning of なんだ is "What is X?" However it can also be used to express the speaker's slight surprise。 Used only in very casual conversation.
昨日[きのう]は 疲[つか]れていたから、 1[いち]日[にち]中[ちゅう] ほとんど 寝[ね]ていました。
I was tired yesterday, so I slept almost all day long.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
ほとんど V Means "almost all; most of (it, the time, etc.)" It is only used with the amount of something is the issue.
デートを し始[はじ]めて、 彼[かれ]の ことが ますます 好[す]きになった。
I've come to like him even more since we started dating.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

ますます Adv "more and more; -er and -er; increasingly; even more; even -er; still more; still -er" ますます occurs with verbs, the adverbial forms of adjectives and adverbs. It indicates that something happens to an even greater (or lesser) degree than before. ますます is NOT used for future controllable events. For example, it cannot replace もっともっと in もっともっとがんばって下さい。
この 映画[えいが]、 面白[おもしろ] そうなんだけど、 一緒[いっしょ]に 見[み]に 行[い]かない？
This movie looks interesting. Do you want to go see it with me?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: S んだけど／ですが is used as a preliminary remark by the speaker to inform the hearer of the speaker's desire, the current situation, etc. before (a) asking a question related to that desire, (b) asking for an opinion on the matter, or (c) making a request. This phrase can also be used to extend an invitation or an offer. When making a request, the request is often unstated, as shown below. んだけど is more casual than んですが. --- 英訳 [English translation]: but (in english, null in most situations) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜ん{だけど/ですが}
両親[りょうしん]は 20[にじゅう]年[ねん] 前[まえ]、 つまり、 私[わたし]の 生[う]まれた 年[とし]に 結婚[けっこん] した。
My parents got married 20 years ago - that is, in the year that I was born.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1/NP1, つまり、N2/NP2 "That is (to say); in other words; namely; (that) means; you mean ~?" つまりis used to rephrase or restate what has just been mentioned or stated.
暖[あたた]かくなるに つれて、 雪[ゆき]が 溶[と]け、 木[き]が 緑[みどり]に なっていく。
As it becomes warmer, the snow is melting and the trees are turning green.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-non-past.aff につれて "as ~; with ~" Xにつれて indicates that omething takes place as X occurs. X can be either a verb or the stem of a suru-V.
寝[ね]られなくなるので、 私[わたし]は ほとんど コーヒーは 飲[の]まない。
It keeps me from sleeping, so I almost never drink coffee.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
ほとんどの N means Almost all N; most of N
私[わたし]は 彼[かれ]の ことが 小[しょう]学校[がっこう]の 時[とき]から ずっと 好[す]きだったんです。
I've liked him ever since elementary school.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

ずっと "all the time; all along; all the way; all through ~; throughout~; ever (since); never (since)" ずっと means that a state or action is ongoing, from one point in time to another point in time (often the moment of speech)

It is used primarily in written language. --- 英訳 [English translation]: must; I'm sure/certain that ~; It is certain that ~; I'm certain that ~; be sure to V. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜に違いない
家賃[やちん]が 上[あ]がったので、 引[ひ]っ越[こ]さなければならない ことに なってしまった。
The rent went up, which means that I've ended up having to move.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S(という)ことになる Means: end up (with); mean that ~; cause This grammar is usually preceded by 1 of 3 types of sentences, here is is (2) reason clause, and indicates that the (non-) action, even or situation stated in the preceding phrase/clause leads to a logical conclusion or a certain situation.
こんなに たくさんの 人[ひと]が 読[よ]んでいるのだから、 面白[おもしろ]い 本[ほん]であるに 違[ちが]い ない。
With this many people reading it, it must be an interesting book.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

〜である/~ではない is the formal plain form of だ and can be affixed to nouns and -な／-の adjectives. である is used in formal writing. In very formal speech the polite form であります／ではありません may be used. である can occur before nouns in relative clauses while だ cannot.
彼[かれ]と 別[わか]れても がっかり する こと ないよ。 もっと いい 人[ひと]が すぐ 見[み]つかるから。
You don't have to be down just because you broke up with your boyfriend. You'll meet someone much better in no time.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-plain.non-past すること（は）ない "don't have to ~; don't need to ~; It's not necessary to ~; There is no need to ~" In casual conversation the は may drop.
絶対[ぜったい]に 怒[おこ]らない 人[ひと]が いるのだろうか。 私[わたし]は 絶対[ぜったい]に そんな 人[ひと]は いないと 思[おも]う。
I wonder if there really are people who never get mad. I definitely don't think people like that exist.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
（そんな／あんな／こんな）N そんな／あんな： Means: that kind of ~; ~like that あんな： Means: this kind of ~; ~ like this these words are synonymous with そういう、ああいう、こういう respectively and are a bit more colloquial than them.
あの アパートには 大学[だいがく]生[せい]が たくさん 住[す]んでいるから、 うるさいに 違[ちが]い ない。
There are a lot of college students living in that apartment, so it must be noisy.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure indicates that the speaker is certain that something is true or is the case. It is used primarily in written language. --- 英訳 [English translation]: must; I'm sure/certain that ~; It is certain that ~; I'm certain that ~; be sure to V. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜に違いない
梅雨[つゆ]に 入[はい]ってから、 晴[は]れの 日[ひ]が まったく なくて 湿度[しつど]が 高[たか]く、 気持[きも]ちが 悪[わる]い。
Since the rainy season began, it's been uncomfortable, with no sunny days and lots of humidity.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N (time period) に {入り/入って (から)} "since N began; after N began" N に入る literally means "to enter N," but when N is a noun indicating a time period, the phrase means "N begins." The most common form is N に入り or N に入って（から), meaning "since/after N began."
ダイエットを しているから、 甘[あま]い 物[もの]は なるべく 食[た]べない ようにしています。
I'm on a diet, so I'm trying to eat as few sweets as I can.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: なるべく with or without an adverb modifies the following verb phrase and adds the meaning "as (much) as possible." When there is no specific adverb after なるべく, it is usually interpreted as "as much as~" or "as often as~." --- 英訳 [English translation]: as much/often as possible; as ~ as possible --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ なるべく
あの 人[ひと]は 動物[どうぶつ]の 言葉[ことば]が 分[わ]かるんです。 猫[ねこ]や 犬[いぬ]とさえ 会話[かいわ]が できるんですよ。
That person can understand what animals say. He can even communicate with cats and dogs.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N (prt) さえ Means: even さえ is an emphatic particle. In non-conditional clauses it means "even." When さえ is used, the particle が never occurs, を usually does not occur, へ and the directional に are optional, and the other particles, including the LOCATIONAL に, で、と and から are mandatory.
広島[ひろしま]県[けん]には 戦争[せんそう]の 恐[おそ]ろしさと 平和[へいわ]の 大切[たいせつ]さを 伝[つた]える 原爆[げんばく] ドームが 有[あ]ります。
Hiroshima Prefecture has the Atomic Bomb Dome, which conveys the horror of war and the importance of peace.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The suffix さ is attached to the stem of an i-adjective or a na-adjective to form a noun. The typical effect is the addition of this suffix "-ness," as in "niceness" or "-ty," as in "rarity." --- 英訳 [English translation]: -ness; -ty --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {A-stem / ANa} + さ: ひろい + さ = ひろさ; さむい + さ = さむさ; 元気さ; 便利さ; (Exception: いい = よさ)
自分[じぶん]で、 部屋[へや]は、 毎日[まいにち]ちゃんと 掃除[そうじ] して、 きちんと 片付[かたづ]けておきなさいよ。
You need to clean your room yourself properly and put things in their proper places every day.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

ちゃんと；きちんと "neatly; tidily; properly; adequately; in good order; regularly; without fail" ちゃんと and きちんと both indicate that someone does something neatly, properly, regularly, or without fail (i.e. in the way it is supposed to be done). ちゃんと is more colloquial than きちんと。
日本[にほん]の 国土[こくど]は 狭[せま] そうに 思[おも]われているが、 数字[すうじ]の 上[うえ]で 見[み]ると、 そうでも ない。
People think of Japan as having a small landmass, but when you look at the numbers, that's not quite the case.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N のうえで "in terms of; from the viewpoint of ~; as far as ~ is concerned; according to ~" Nの上で and N上 are used to indicate that the speaker's statement refers only to N. Commonly used in written language.
アメリカでは、 お酒[さけ]が 飲[の]める 年齢[ねんれい]に ついての 規制[きせい]は、 各州[かくしゅう]で それぞれ 違[ちが]う。
In the United States, the rules concerning the legal drinking age are different in each state.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
各 + N "each ~; various" A prefix which adds the meaning "each; various." When the referent of the noun after 各 is unknown, it means "various."
一人[ひとり]で するのが 大変[たいへん]な 場合[ばあい]は、 クラスメートと 一緒[いっしょ]に 宿題[しゅくだい]を しても いいです。
If it's too difficult to do alone, it's all right to work on your homework with your classmates.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 場合 is a noun meaning "case, occasion, situation," but with a modifier it forms an adverbial phrase/clause meaning "when; if; in case." 時 can be used in place of 場合 as seen in this example: 分からない {時／場合} は、言って下さい。 However, 場合 cannot replace 時 when 時 refers to a specific time and does not mean "case; occasion; situation," as shown in the example below: 私が行った {時／ｘ場合}には、ミーティングが始まっていた。 --- 英訳 [English translation]: if; when; in case --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ DemA + 場合: {この/その/あの} 場合
彼女[かのじょ]の 第[だい]一[いち] 印象[いんしょう]は 悪[わる]かったのに、 なぜか 私[わたし]と 彼女[かのじょ]は とても いい 友達[ともだち]に なった。
My first impression of her was bad, but for some reason she and I became really good friends.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
第一 N "first; first of all; to begin with; the first; the primary"
彼[かれ]らが 言[い]っている ことは よく 分[わ]からない。 私[わたし]たちの 考[かんが]えに 反対[はんたい]なのだろうか。
I don't really understand what they're saying. I wonder if they are disagreeing with our idea.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

Personal pronoun ら "these; those; they; -s; and others" [plural dem. pronouns can be used in polite speech] The plural marker ら is often used with demonstrative pronouns and certain personal pronouns. plural personal pronouns are not used in polite speech.
ルームメートは、 毎日[まいにち] 寝[ね]てばっかり いる。 授業[じゅぎょう]に 行[い]かなくても いいのかなあ。
My roommate does nothing but sleep every day. I wonder if it's OK for him not to go to class.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V−te ばかりいる。 Means: Nothing But; always; all the time ばかり is used to express the idea that someone does one thing all the time and does nothing else, or that someone chooses just one thing among others when doing something. Ex: 田中さんはマンガばかり読んでいる。 can mean: (= All tanaka does is read comics); (= Tanaka reads only comics); (=When Masao reads, he reads nothing but comics) NOTE: ばっかり is more colloquial than ばかり
あの 殺人[さつじん] 事件[じけん]から もう 5[ご]年[ねん]も たっているのに、 未[いま]だに 犯人[はんにん]は 捕[つか]まっていない。
It's been five years since that murder (case), but the killer still hasn't been caught.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
未だに "still; (not ~) yet" indicates that someone of something is in the same state as he/she/it was some time ago. This form is primarily used in written language. In spoken language まだ is used.
環境[かんきょう]を よく する ため、 来月[らいげつ]から リサイクル キャンペーンを する ことに なった。
In an effort to improve the environment, it's been decided that as of next month we'll begin a recycling campaign.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-non-pastことになった means that a situation has changed due to some external force (e.g. a decision made by someone other than the speaker). It indicates either that the speaker (or the subject of the sentence) did not actively make the decision or that he/she is viewing the decision from the standpoint of an outsider. Note that ことにした indicates that the speaker or the subject made a decision to do something. --- 英訳 [English translation]: It was/has been decided that ~; It turns out that~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-non-past.plain-ことになった:{行く/行かない}ことになった
この 猫[ねこ]、 拾[ひろ]ってきた ときは 死[し]に そうだったけど、 だんだん 元気[げんき]になったんだ。
When I took in this abandoned cat, it was close to dying, but little by little it's gotten healthier.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
だんだん "gradually; little by little; bit by bit" だんだん is used to indicate that a state changes gradually. Thus, it often occurs with ~ていく; 〜てくる；〜くなる；〜になる；〜ようになる
疲[つか]れていたので、 電気[でんき]を つけた まま 寝[ね]てしまった。 ネクタイも した ままだった。
I was tired, so I fell asleep with the lights still on. I left my tie on, too.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
Aまま（で）V "V with ~; V while ~; V as (it is); V without ~" まま indicates that the state of X remains unchanged or that someone does something without changing the current state of X.
引[ひ]っ越[こ]す 前[まえ]は、 アパートの 前[まえ]の 道[みち]が こんなに うるさい ことに 気[き]が つかなかった。
Before I moved in, I didn't realize that the street in front of the apartment was this noisy.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S ことに気がつく means: notice (that~); realize that ~ Notice that the presence of こと in a sentence using this grammar may not always be the nominalizer meaning "that." It could be a noun meaning "thing" following the noun-typed usage of this grammar.
なぜ 彼[かれ]は 私[わたし]の ことを 愛[あい]してくれないのだろうか。 私[わたし]は 彼[かれ]が こんなに 好[す]きなのに。
I wonder why he doesn't love me back, even though I love him so much.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
Sの（だろう／でしょう）か Means: I wonder ~ Indicates a self-addressed question which can either be a yes-no question or a wh- question.
この サイトでは、 iPodの ユーザー同士[どうし]が 意見[いけん]を 交換[こうかん] し合[あ]う ことが できます。
At this site, iPod users can exchange opinions with each other.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N同士 {が／で／を} Indicates that Ns do something together, that Ns do something to/for/against each other, or that someone puts Ns together in some way.
今朝[けさ]、 朝寝[あさね]坊[ぼう] して クラスに 遅[おく]れちゃったから、 明日[あした]は もっと 早[はや]く 起[お]きなくちゃ。
This morning I overslept and ended up being late for class, so I've gotta wake up earlier tomorrow.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: These patterns express the idea of obligation. Although the two patterns are interchangeable, there is a subtle difference between ならない and いけない. That is, ならない is commonly used when the speaker states his/her sense of obligation while いけない is commonly used when the sense of obligation is directed towards the hearer (i.e. when the speaker wants to impose a certain obligation on the hearer). The following contracted forms are used in casual conversation: なきゃならない -> なきゃなんない なくちゃならない -> なくちゃんなんない --- 英訳 [English translation]: have to; must; should --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜なければ{いけない/ならない} 〜なくては{いけない/ならない}
フィンランド語[ご]とか トルコ語[ご]とか、 皆[みな]が 余[あま]り 勉強[べんきょう] してない 言葉[ことば]を 勉強[べんきょう] してみたい。
I want to try studying a language not many people learn, like Finnish or Turkish.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: とか is used to list examples non-exhaustively. It is similar to や in meaning when the examples listed are nouns. Unlike や, however, とか can be preceeded by verb phrases. When two or more items are listed, とか after the final item is optional when it is followed by a particle and mandatory otherwise (like in this example). (Note that や does not occur after the final item). In Subject とか Subject とかする, the final とか is not optional. --- 英訳 [English translation]: things/places/etc. like ~; and; or --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Noun とか Noun (とか) b. Sentence-plain とか Sentence-plain とか {する/できる}
スミスさんは 日本[にほん]に １０[じゅう]年[ねん]も 住[す]んでいたから、 日本[にほん]語[ご]が 上手[じょうず]に 話[はな]せるに 違[ちが]い ない。
Smith has spent as many as 10 years living in Japan, so Smith must be able to speak Japanese well.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure indicates that the speaker is certain that something is true or is the case. It is used primarily in written language. --- 英訳 [English translation]: must; I'm sure/certain that ~; It is certain that ~; I'm certain that ~; be sure to V. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜に違いない
キッチンから 流[なが]れてくる においから すると、 今日[きょう]の 晩御飯[ばんごはん]は カレー ライスかなあ。
The smell from the kitchen makes me think we're having curry tonight.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
Nからすると "judging from~" Introduces the source or basis for the speaker's conjecture or judgment. The information can be of any sort including visual or verbal.
動物[どうぶつ]園[えん]で パンダの 赤[あか]ちゃんが ３[さん]匹[びき] 生[う]まれた そうだ。 こう いう ニュースは うれしい。
I hear that three baby pandas were born at the zoo. This kind of news makes me happy.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (1) When そういう, こういう and ああいう refer to something/someone the speaker sees or perceives, they are used for something/someone close to the hearer, close to the speaker, and away from both the speaker and the hearer respectively. (2) These phrases are also used to refer to something/someone the speaker or the hearer has just mentioned. Specifically, そういう is used when the speaker has just mentioned something/someone. こういう is used when the speaker has just stated something factual about something/someone. And ああいう is used when the information the speaker or the hearer has just mentioned is known to both. --- 英訳 [English translation]: that/this kind of; such --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {そう/こう/ああ}いうN
私[わたし]の 弟[おとうと]は １[いっ]歳[さい]の 時[とき]、 歩[ある]き始[はじ]めました。 そして、 １[いっ]歳[さい] 半[はん]に 成[な]った 時[とき]、 話[はな]し始[はじ]めました。
My little brother started walking when he was one year old, and then he started talking when he was one and a half.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
説明 [explanation]: 始める in this use is an auxiliary verb meaning "begin to V." --- 英訳 [English translation]: begin to, begin-V-ing --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Verb-masu 始める
健康[けんこう]の ためには、 朝御飯[あさごはん]は ちゃんと 食[た]べて、 夜[よる]も 6[ろく]時間[じかん] 以上[いじょう] はねた 方[ほう]が いいですよ。
For your health, you'd better eat a proper breakfast every morning and sleep at least six hours every night.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

ちゃんと；きちんと "neatly; tidily; properly; adequately; in good order; regularly; without fail" ちゃんと and きちんと both indicate that someone does something neatly, properly, regularly, or without fail (i.e. in the way it is supposed to be done). ちゃんと is more colloquial than きちんと。
急[いそ]いでいたので タクシーに 乗[の]ったら、 道[みち]が 混[こ]んでいて、 かえって 遅[おそ]くなってしまった。
I took a taxi because I was in a hurry, but the roads were crowded and I ended up even later than I would have been otherwise.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
かえって "on the contrary; rather"
今[いま]、 ちょっと 忙[いそが]しくて、 電話[でんわ]で 話[はな]してられないから、 後[あと]で 私[わたし]から かけなおしても いい？
I'm a little busy right now, so I can't talk on the phone any longer. Can I call you back later?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-masu 直す "again, re-V" 直す, when attached to the masu-stems of verbs, creates compound verbs with the meaning "again; re-."
東京[とうきょう]は 物価[ぶっか]が 高[たか]い ことだけでなく、 土地[とち]も 狭[せま]いので、 暮[く]らしにくいと いうのは 事実[じじつ]だ。
The fact is that Tokyo is a hard place to live in, not only because the prices are high there but also because the land is cramped.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S (という）のは事実だ。 "It is {true/a fact that} ~" Used when the speaker wants to claim that something is true or is a fact, or when he/she admits that something is true or a fact. The presence or absence of という does not change the meaning.
日本[にほん]語[ご]には 「いらっしゃいます」や 「召[め]し上[あ]がります」など、 いろいろな 敬語[けいご]が ある。
In Japanese, there are various honorific expressions, like irasshaimasu and meshiagarimasu.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: など indicates that the given list is not exhaustive. When more than one item is listed, や is commonly used to connect the item. --- 英訳 [English translation]: N1やN2など = N1, N2 and others. N1やN2などのN3 = N3 such as N1 and N2; N3 like N1 and N2. N1やN2など、N3 = N3 such as N1 and N2; N3 like N1 and N2. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N1やN2など({は / も / が / を / に / の / etc.)} (N1 and N2 can be words or phrases).
授業[じゅぎょう]を 休[やす]む ときは 先生[せんせい]に 連絡[れんらく] しなくては いけない ことに なっているが、 忘[わす]れてしまった。
We're supposed to let the teacher know if we're going to miss a class, but I forgot.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-plain.non-past ことになっている means that something has been decided and the result of the decision is still in effect. It is often used to introduce rules or customs, as well as one's schedule. --- 英訳 [English translation]: be supposed to ~; It is a rule that ~; It's been decided that ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.non-past ことになっている: {行く/行かない}ことになっている
